ops.title: Operations overview
ops.noAirlineHint: Found your own airline: choose a name, colours, a home airport and your starting capital.
ops.notInstalled: Not yet: use “Add to Home Screen” / “Install”

modeHint.realtime: Time runs continuously. Pause any time; choose a speed from 1 game minute to 1 game day per second.
modeHint.weekly: Time stands still while you decide. “End week” simulates the next 7 days in one go.

newGame.title: Found your airline
newGame.intro: A startup in 2026. Choose your identity, home base and money – then lease your first aircraft.
newGame.name: Airline name
newGame.codesHint: The 2-character code goes in front of flight numbers (like OS 51), the 3-letter ICAO code is used by air traffic control.
newGame.hubHint: Your books are kept in {{currency}}. Aircraft leases are priced in US dollars, as in the real industry.

capitalHint.tight: Like a very small startup: one or two aircraft, every mistake hurts.
capitalHint.standard: Roughly what real low-cost startups raised: a small fleet to start.
capitalHint.funded: A startup with strong investors behind it: room for wide-bodies.

newGame.laterHint: Hardcore realism, historical start years, the Austrian Airlines takeover and competitors arrive in later phases.
newGame.replaceWarning: You already have a game running. Founding a new airline replaces it.

fleet.title: Fleet
fleet.noGame: Found an airline first, then you can lease aircraft here.
fleet.empty: You have no aircraft yet. Lessors are offering used aircraft on the lease market.
fleet.marketIntro: Used aircraft offered by leasing companies. You pay a security deposit now; monthly rent starts on delivery. New offers appear at the start of each month, old ones expire.
fleet.leased: Lease signed! Your {{type}} will be registered as {{registration}}.
fleet.runwayWarning: Fully loaded, this type needs {{needed}} m of runway; {{hub}} has {{runway}} m. It can still fly shorter routes with less fuel.
fleet.confirmText_one: Pay a deposit of {{deposit}} now. Rent of {{rent}} per month starts on delivery ({{date}}) and runs for {{count}} year.
fleet.confirmText_other: Pay a deposit of {{deposit}} now. Rent of {{rent}} per month starts on delivery ({{date}}) and runs for {{count}} years.

network.title: Network
network.intro: Your routes from the hub. Simple scheduling: you choose aircraft and round trips per week, the game sets the departure times.
network.empty: No routes yet. Open your first route to start flying.
network.maxFrequency_one: This aircraft has room for {{count}} more round trip.
network.maxFrequency_other: This aircraft has room for up to {{count}} round trips.
network.noCompetition: no airline flies this route non-stop
network.fixedNote: Not included: crew salaries and lease for {{registration}} ({{cost}} per week), which all routes of this aircraft share, and the airline's overheads. The route uses {{hours}} block hours per week.
network.forecastNote: Forecast for this month's season once the route is known; new routes start with about 60 % of these passengers and grow over 8 weeks. Summer is busier than winter, and fuel prices change every week. Other airlines react to your prices and timetable within about a month.
network.closeConfirm: Close this route? Flights stop immediately.
network.plusConnections: Plus one-stop connections via other hubs.
network.introDetailed: Your routes from the hub with your own timetable: every flight has a departure time, days of operation and an aircraft.
network.fixedNoteDetailed: Not included: crew salaries and leases of {{registration}} ({{cost}} per week together), which they share with their other routes, and the airline's overheads. The route uses {{hours}} block hours per week.

finance.title: Finance
finance.cashNote: Ticket revenue and flight costs are booked every day; lease rents leave on the 1st of each month.
finance.pnlNote: Lease costs are spread over the days of the month here, even though the cash leaves once a month. Overheads are paid from the day the airline is founded, even without aircraft.
finance.directNote: Route result = ticket revenue minus fuel, maintenance, fees, handling and sales. Crews and leases are paid per aircraft, not per route.
finance.chartHint: Green = profit, red = loss, light = period still running. Tap a bar to see that period in detail; swipe sideways for older periods. Weeks are kept for two years, months for the whole game.

airlines.title: Airlines
airlines.intro: The real airlines of the world ({{count}} with a known network). Biggest first; search by name, code or hub.
airlines.search: Search airline, code or hub (e.g. OS, Ryanair, VIE)

colorSource.generated: generated colours (real colours not yet entered)

airlines.networkNote: Routes from Wikipedia's airport articles. Weekly flights: official Eurostat totals (season {{season}}); where several airlines share a route, the total is split between them (an estimate, marked “modelled”), and routes without official numbers are filled in by the game's demand model.
airlines.closedRoutes_one: {{count}} route given up in this game.
airlines.closedRoutes_other: {{count}} routes given up in this game.

sources.title: Data sources
sources.intro: This game is built on open data. Thank you to everyone who collects and shares it. Real airlines appear with their names and colours, never with their logos.
sources.notes: Wikipedia-based data in this game is published under CC BY-SA 4.0 (share-alike). Full list with download dates and how each dataset is processed: docs/DATA_SOURCES.md in the game's GitHub repository.

tagHint.official: From official statistics or registers (e.g. Eurostat, FAA).
tagHint.hand-checked: Checked by hand against the airline's own information.
tagHint.modelled: Estimated by the game's demand model where no real number is available.

use.ourairports: All airports with scheduled flights: position, runways, size.
use.geonames: City populations (catchment and market size) and time zones.
use.worldbank: Wealth (GDP per person) and tourism per country.
use.naturalearth: Coastlines and borders of the map.
use.openfreemap: Fonts for the airport codes on the map.
use.wikipedia: Which airline flies where (airport articles), airline business models, hubs, bases, fleets and seat layouts (airline articles).
use.wikidata: Airline names, codes, countries, alliances and parent companies; links between articles and airports.
use.eurostat: Real passenger numbers, seats and flights per route in Europe (summer 2024), used for demand and for the airlines' weekly flights.
use.eia: The real jet fuel price, week by week in 2026.
use.faa: Individual aircraft (registration, type, year) of US airlines.
use.austrocontrol: Individual aircraft of Austrian airlines, including the operator.
use.iaa: Individual aircraft of Irish airlines (Ryanair, Aer Lingus).
use.manufacturers: Aircraft performance: seats, range, take-off distance, weight.

timetable.title: Timetable

mode.simple: Simple scheduling: the game sets the times.

modeHint.simple: You choose round trips per week; the game plans departure times (from 06:00 hub time). You can switch to Detailed later.
modeHint.detailed: You set every flight yourself: departure time, days of operation, aircraft and ground time — like a real airline's network planning.

timetable.switchConfirm: Switch to detailed scheduling? Your current flights become a timetable you can edit. This cannot be undone.
timetable.hint: Times are local: departure in {{hub}} time, the return in {{dest}} time. The ground time includes unloading, cleaning, catering and boarding (at least the aircraft's minimum turnaround); 8 hours or more is a night stop.
timetable.boardNote: Local times at each airport. Days: 1 = Monday … 7 = Sunday, as in airline timetables; +1 = arrives the next day.
timetable.timesNote: Passengers choose by departure time: business travellers want early mornings out and evenings back, holidaymakers are flexible but avoid night flights; Fridays and Sundays are busier than Tuesdays. Flights close to a competitor's (or your own) share their passengers. Eastbound flights are faster (westerly winds). Competitors' times are generated by the game (real times may not be copied), marked “modelled”; * = not every day.

timeline.title: Week of {{registration}} (hub time)
timeline.label: Rotation chart of {{registration}}
timeline.note: Each row is a day in hub local time: flight out, time at the destination (light), flight back, turnaround (faint). Magenta = the route you are editing, red = collision.

saves.title: Saves
saves.intro: Every game has its own save slot on this device and saves itself automatically. Keep copies to go back to, and export files as a backup or to continue on another device.
saves.autosave: Saved automatically: when you pause, change something, leave the app, and every 15 seconds while the clock runs.
saves.restoreConfirm: Go back to “{{name}}”? The game continues from this copy; progress made since then is lost unless you save a copy of it first.
saves.deleteGameConfirm_one: Delete the game “{{name}}” and its copy from this device? Exported files are not affected.
saves.deleteGameConfirm_other: Delete the game “{{name}}” and its {{count}} copies from this device? Exported files are not affected.
saves.importFailed: This file is not a save from this game (or it is damaged).
saves.loadFailed: This save could not be opened.
saves.failed: Something went wrong while saving or reading.
saves.exportNote: Export creates a small compressed “.amsave” file. To continue on another device, send it there (e.g. by e-mail or cloud drive) and use “Import file”. Cloud sync comes in Phase 3.
saves.storage: Storage used by the game: {{used}} MB of about {{quota}} MB.
saves.persisted: The browser keeps these saves permanently.
saves.notPersisted: The browser may delete them if space runs low: export a backup now and then (installing the app helps).

dashboard.title: Key figures
dashboard.period: Last full week, from {{week}}; ▲▼ = change against the week before, line = last 12 weeks (point at it for values).
dashboard.waiting: The key figures appear after your first full week of flying (weeks run Monday to Sunday).

hint.cash: Money in the bank. Below zero, the airline is in trouble.
hint.result: Revenue minus all costs (incl. crews, leases, overheads) in the last full week.
hint.margin: Result as a share of revenue. Good European airlines make 5–15 % over a year.
hint.loadFactor: Share of seat-km sold (RPK ÷ ASK). European airlines: about 80–90 %.
hint.rask: Revenue per available seat-km: what each seat flown one km earns.
hint.cask: Cost per available seat-km (all costs). Earns money when RASK is higher.
hint.caskExFuel: CASK without fuel: the costs the airline controls itself.
hint.yield: Revenue per passenger-km: the average price per km flown.
hint.utilisation: Block hours per aircraft per day. Short-haul airlines: about 9–12 h.

dashboard.note: Route results here are before crews, leases and overheads. Utilisation uses today's number of aircraft.

cabin.summary: {{seats}} seats of {{max}} allowed by the exits · {{used}} % of the cabin length used
cabin.expected: Passengers expect about {{score}} in this class
cabin.comfortNote: Rating of the seat on short and long flights (0–100). Green: as good as passengers expect of this class, amber: a bit worse, red: much worse. Pitch = distance from one seat to the same point of the seat in front. European business has a movable curtain: on each flight, rows business doesn't need are sold as economy.
cabin.freeBeforeDelivery: Free: the aircraft isn't delivered yet, the lessor fits the new cabin during the transition.
cabin.quote: Refit: {{cost}}, {{days}} days in the hangar ({{seats}} new seats). Paid now, written off over 6 years. The aircraft's flights are cancelled during the refit.

reputation.title: Reputation
reputation.scoreHint: What passengers say about you (0–100, 60 = as expected). Built slowly, week by week, from every passenger's trip. For comparison, real airlines in the game: network carriers {{legacy}}, low-cost {{lowcost}} (modelled).
reputation.awarenessHint: How well known you are in your markets. It grows with the passengers you carry; unknown airlines win fewer travellers.
reputation.noRatings: No ratings yet: they come in with your first passengers.
reputation.note: Last week's passengers: points compared with what they expect of the class. Seat = seat product and pitch; aircraft = age (new is nicer); price = value for money; crowding = very full cabins. Punctuality and service join in Phase 9.
